narrative.overview:
CCM Portal is browsed like a catalogue you already know how to use. Every request is a typeset title card: its name set as heavy display lettering on a flat tile, a narrow strip of field cells running down its left edge, the creator and the time left at its foot. Cards sit in horizontal shelves that scroll and let the next title peek at the edge. When a title is focused it widens in place to show its fields, and the rest of the wall steps back a tone. The most urgent request is featured above the shelves as a billboard, the largest lettering on the screen.

The world is one dark theme, pinned, for staff who review creator uploads late at night in dim rooms and for creators on their phones. Depth comes from tone steps on a deep neutral ground, never from shadow at rest. Colour is scarce on purpose: a single marquee yellow marks keyboard focus and the one primary action in a region, and the field-state hues (to-do grey, ready blue, needs-changes orange, overdue red, approved green) live only inside tiles, strips and the chips that sit in them. Every state is a colour, an icon and a word together, never colour alone. There is no brand green: green means Approved and nothing else.

Discretion is part of the look. Uploads never show until someone chooses to reveal them; request titles never leave the app through tab titles, texts or email subjects. Dates and countdowns all read on one agency clock. The old green shadcn look, gradients, glass, glows and the KPI-row-over-a-table dashboard are rejected.
keyCharacteristics: One pinned dark theme: ground #0e0f12, tiles #1b1d22, every surface one tone step from the next.
Titles set as display lettering in Onest 800 with -0.035em tracking, sized by their length, two lines at most.
One accent, marquee yellow, for focus and the one primary action per region.
Field-state colour lives only inside tiles; the coloured spine is the request title card's alone.
Shelves of fractional width so the next tile always peeks; focus widens a title in place.
Flat at rest; soft shadows only on true overlays.
Previews hidden until revealed; no request title in any channel that leaves the app.

rules.name: The One Marquee Rule
rules.body: Yellow appears only as the focus outline and as the fill of the one primary action in a region. When a page-level create action (New request) would compete with a region's yellow, it takes the light ink fill instead. Pressed, selected and current states are tone steps, never yellow.

rules.name: The Green Means Approved Rule
rules.body: There is no brand green. Green appears only as Approved Green, on things that are approved (field cells, upload and request chips, the approved count), always with its check icon and the word. Success toasts and "saved" confirmations are neutral (Confirm Silver); switches and checkboxes turn on in ink; buttons, chrome and navigation are never green. Green also survives as one choice in user-pickable data palettes (tags, groups, annotations), which are data, not brand.

rules.name: The States Stay Inside Rule
rules.body: Ready blue, changes orange, late red and approved green appear only inside tiles, field strips, and chips that sit in rows or tiles, and always with their icon and word (never colour alone). Page chrome, headings, navigation and buttons never carry a state hue; destructive actions use a late-red tint, not a red slab.

rules.name: The Lettering Rule
rules.body: A title is set, not written: Onest 800, tracking -0.035em, sized by its length, never more than two lines, balanced. Nothing else in the interface uses 800.

rules.name: The Heading First Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a heading: no eyebrow, kicker or overline. Context (kind, sender, "sent 15 days ago", "404") goes in a line under the title. Headings and labels are sentence case; nothing is set in tracked uppercase.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number is tabular: body, tables, times and countdowns set `tabular-nums` so figures do not jitter as they tick.

rules.name: The Tone Step Rule
rules.body: If it does not float, it has no shadow. Lift a surface by moving it one tone step, never by adding a shadow, a glow, glass or a gradient. The one gradient in the world is the billboard plate's mask, which fades a flat tile into the ground (horizontally on desktop, vertically under 900px) rather than blending colours.

rules.name: The Only Spine Rule
rules.body: The vertical strip of field cells down the left edge of a request title card is the only coloured edge in the system. Creator cards, template cards, message cards, alerts and list rows never take a coloured side stripe.

rules.name: The Discretion Rule
rules.body: Request titles can be explicit, so they never leave the app: tab titles on request pages are generic ("Request · CCM Portal"), SMS bodies carry no title, and email subjects and preheaders carry no title. Upload previews stay hidden, with no image request, until a person reveals them.

rules.name: The Agency Clock Rule
rules.body: Every date, due line and countdown is formatted through the display-timezone helpers in `src/components/title-wall/time.ts`, never the machine's local time. A plain date is due at 23:59 on that day in the agency's timezone; a timestamp is used as is.

dos: **Do** set every surface as a tone step on the ground: tile for content, tile-hi for hover and focus, raised for overlays, well for inputs.
**Do** give each region exactly one yellow primary action, and use the light ink button for a page-level create action when yellow is taken.
**Do** draw keyboard focus as a 2px yellow outline (1.5px inset on title cards) on everything interactive.
**Do** set titles in Onest 800 at -0.035em, sized by length, two lines at most, with the billboard title the largest type on the screen.
**Do** open each page with its title and one sentence that answers the screen's question, with context lines under headings.

**Do** show field state with cells, spines, labelled strips and tinted chips inside tiles, with the state's icon and word wherever it is written out; take colours, icons and words from the shared vocabulary, never hard-code them.
**Do** keep shelves at fractional widths so the next tile peeks, and step the rest of the wall back to tile-dim without dimming its text.
**Do** route every date and countdown through `src/components/title-wall/time.ts`, and turn countdowns red only when late or under 48 hours.
**Do** keep previews hidden until revealed and keep request titles out of tab titles, SMS bodies and email subjects.
**Do** keep controls 40 to 44px on touch and 36px from 768px, with 16px input text on phones.
donts: **Don't** use green for anything but Approved: not for success toasts, "saved", switches, checkboxes, buttons or brand. Never show a state by colour alone.
**Don't** use yellow for selected, pressed or current states, for decoration, or for more than one action per region.
**Don't** put state hues in page chrome, headings, navigation or buttons; destructive actions are a tint, not a red slab.
**Don't** put a coloured edge stripe on anything but a request title card.
**Don't** place an eyebrow, kicker or overline above a heading, or set labels in tracked uppercase.
**Don't** add a light theme, a theme toggle, gradients, glass, glows or a shadow on anything that does not float.
**Don't** build a KPI row over a table; counts go in a sentence and a quiet counts line.
**Don't** format dates with the browser's or server's local timezone.
**Don't** render an upload thumbnail before the person reveals it.
